News.title: Tesco urgently recalls popular meat product due to ‘deadly bacteria’ telling shoppers ‘do not eat’
News.content:
TOTAL RECALL Tesco urgently recalls popular meat product due to ‘deadly bacteria’ telling shoppers ‘do not eat’

TESCO has issued an urgent recall for a cooked meat product, warning customers “do not eat”.

The UK Food Standards Agency (FSA) has warned the British Bresaola may be potentially carrying traces of a dangerous bacteria.



The Curing Barn is recalling the meat over contamination with Listeria monocytogenes.

This is a type of pathogenic bacteria that can cause listeriosis.



Listeriosis is a rare but potentially very serious illness.

It can cause a high temperature, muscle ache or pain, chills, sickness and diarrhoea.

In extremely rare cases, the bacteria can even lead to meningitis.

The bacterial infection is particularly dangerous for those over the age of 65, pregnant women, or individuals with a weakened immune system.



Bresaola is an aged, air-dried beef, based on an Italian delicacy.

It is currently retailed at £4.50 per packet, and can be found in supermarkets like Tesco.

The potentially harmful product that is being recalled will have a use by date of June 10 2026.

It also has the product code ‘WLRC J1Z2 0WD0 J85J’ and is labelled as 60g.



All points of sale will display a recall notice, urging customers to return the goods to the store for a full refund.

The FSA said: “If you have bought the above product, do not eat it. Instead, return it to where you bought it from for a full refund.”

This comes just days after a sandwich meat was recalled from Tesco, ASDA and Morrisons over the same bacterial concerns.

Listeria was identified in the Turkey Breast Pastrami and the FSA issued an urgent recall as a consequence.

The 142 gram packs with the product code CK016 CK027 and the use by date April 9, 2026 are currently affected by this recall.

News.title: Horror moment fire rips through tourist boat in holiday hotspot leaving 5 injured and 1 missing
News.content:
THIS is the horrifying moment a fire rips through a speedboat out on the water – sparking a desperate rescue mission for a missing tour guide.

Five people were injured after an explosion erupted on board the vessel as brave onlookers jumped into the water to try and save those trapped among the flames.





Thick, black plumes of smoke were seen billowing on the holiday island of Phuket in Thailand as an inferno broke out on the speedboat named Tequila.

Workers were reportedly carrying out engine repairs on the boat at the time of the blast.

Footage shows emergency crews battling to contain the flames off Coco Pier at around 10.30am local time.



As workers jumped into the water to help untie the boat and drag those onboard to safety a tour guide who also tried to help went missing.

Komphet Wanadee, 24, reportedly vanished after going underwater as the speedboat was towed away by another vessel until the flames subsided.

Five crew members suffered minor injuries and were rushed to nearby hospitals.

They were identified as Niwat Duangmani, Chutidet Arischa, Muhammad Husam Tiangnoi, Piyathida Pojin and Komkrit Arunadet.



The Phuket City Administrative Office said in a statement: “Five people, including four men and a woman, have been rescued and transported to the hospital.

“One person, a 24-year-old man, is still being searched for.

“Currently, the boat has been towed away to prevent the fire from spreading to other vessels, and the fire is under control by the Phuket Provincial Administrative Organisation’s fire boat.

“Initially, the cause is believed to have been an explosion on the boat.”

Officials have cordoned off the area as divers continue to scour the area for the missing tour guide.



It comes as a mum and her young son died after a speedboat ploughed into a pier and flipped over, trapping those on board under the water earlier this year.

Viviane Aparecida Aredes, 35, and her four-year-old boy, Bento Aredes Ferreira, were among the six victims of the tragic night-time accident in Brazil.

Navigating through the dark, the speedboat driver is suspected of losing control of his vessel and slamming into a pier.

The force of the collision threw some of the passengers backwards as the private boat capsized.

News.title: I was left covered in blood when ‘pocket bully’ savaged my autistic son’s beloved dog to death – the law needs to change
News.content:
A MUM was left traumatised after a pocket bully savaged her autistic son’s therapy dog so badly he had to be put down.

Karen Hawthornthwaite was taking Benji, a tiny Lhasa Apso, for a morning walk when he was suddenly set upon in a brutal attack outside her home in Lancashire.





Benji’s injuries were so severe that his front leg was amputated before Karen was forced to put him to sleep a week later.

The attack took a devastating toll on Karen and her family, and she says she still suffers from the trauma of that day nearly twelve months on.

On the morning of April 29, Karen was taking Benji for his routine walk in the neighbourhood when she spotted a “pocket bully” off its lead.

She told The Sun: “It ran straight into the road, into the main road. I said to myself ‘that dog’s not safe, it’s going to get run over’.

“I couldn’t see anybody with it.”

As Karen arrived home, she was chatting to a neighbour outside her front gate when the horror unfolded.



“Next thing I hear is an almighty shriek,” she recalls.

In horrific CCTV footage, the Bully can be seen off the lead and without a muzzle with its owner before it spots Karen’s beloved family pet from the opposite side of the street.

With Benji in its sights, it races across the road as its owner desperately tries to hold it back.

Unable to stop the dog from attacking, it latches onto Benji’s throat and front leg, violently shaking him from side to side as both Karen and the owner try and pull them apart.

“I can’t even explain what it was like. It just wasn’t letting go,” Karen said.



“The pocket bully’s mouth was covered in blood. Benji was covered in blood. I had blood all over me.”

Her screams alerted her neighbours who tried to intervene to separate the two dogs.

“This fella was just absolutely smacking the hell out of this dog and it wasn’t budging. Another neighbour started hitting it, but nothing,” Karen added.

“There was no control over that dog at all. We were scared ourselves, if he did let go, he’d have gone for one of us.

“Eventually the owner of this dog managed to get him off Benji.”



After screaming at him to get the dog away as it still tried to attack Benji, Karen said the owner returned and apologised saying “she’s never done anything like this before”.

“I said ‘that dog is not right’. I was obviously fuming. I can’t explain what I was feeling. It was just heartbreak,” Karen said.



“My friend heard the scream from the street after and she’d come round, seen me holding Benji and she’s crying.

“She’d seen me crying and she looks at me and I just shook my head saying, ‘it’s not good’.”

Benji was raced to the vets and was “swollen black and blue with blood everywhere”.

His injuries were initially so bad that they “couldn’t even look at him”, and Benji later had to have his front-left leg amputated.

But vets’ efforts were in vain as Karen eventually had to have Benji put to sleep – six years to the day after she had brought him home.



Nearly a year after the attack, Karen says she still suffers from the trauma of what happened.

She said: “I’ve had no sleep for weeks. I’ve had nightmares, flashbacks, you name it.

“As soon as I go out my front door, all I can see near the lamp post is Benji and him looking at me.”

The family later welcomed Luna – a working cocker spaniel – to the family but Karen can no longer do the morning dog walk.



If her husband is away working, she can’t leave the house.

Karen and her husband initially got Benji as a way of trying to get their autistic son Riley, 17, to leave the house.

Benji ended up becoming a therapy dog and he “would come downstairs and play with him”.

“It’s had a massive impact on him. He was absolutely heartbroken,” Karen said.

Cops said the incident didn’t meet “any offences under the Dangerous Dog Act”.



The owner was given an Acceptable Behaviour Contract (ABC) with conditions including keeping the dog on a lead at all times in residential areas.

But Karen argues: “Who’s going to monitor this?”

Her belief is that the bully is dangerous and should have been destroyed after the attack.

She blasted the police as “absolutely useless” after pulling her “from pillar to post” – and she called for changes to the Dangerous Dog Act to also encompass dog-on-dog attacks.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

A spokesperson for Lancashire Police said: “Having thoroughly reviewed all the circumstances and sought expert advice, it was deemed that this incident did not meet the criteria of any offences under the Dangerous Dog Act.



“However, in order to reduce the likelihood of a similar incident happening again, the owner of the pocket bulldog was given an Acceptable Behaviour Contract under the ASB, Crime and Policing Act, 2014 with specific conditions which include ensuring their dog is on a lead at all times in residential areas.”

News.title: Girl, 8 and brother, 5, died after ‘getting trapped in fridge-freezer’ in game of hide-and-seek gone wrong
News.content:
'WORDS FAIL ME' Girl, 8 and brother, 5, died after ‘getting trapped in fridge-freezer’ in game of hide-and-seek gone wrong

TWO young siblings have died after allegedly getting trapped in a fridge-freezer in a game of hide-and-seek gone horribly wrong.

Saori, eight, and her brother Darien, five, were rushed to hospital after their parents discovered them unconscious inside the home appliance.





Tragically, doctors’ attempts to revive them were unsuccessful.

The heartbroken parents said they had popped out to the shops for a quick 20 minute trip when the tragedy unfolded around 7pm Saturday evening.

They had left the young children at home alone in Vista Hermosa, Colombia, not imagining the horror they would come home to.

Dad Brayan Guevara Trivino insisted the freezer was turned off and instead the kids suffocated inside.

He told Colombian daily El Tiempo: “We went out to get groceries and to look for a little shirt they needed for a parade when they started school.”

“We went out and it took us about 20 minutes, more or less. The freezer was unplugged,” he said.

“The children climbed in and got inside. They played, the lid fell, it closed on them and they suffocated.”

He said the children loved playing hide-and-seek – he and his wife even started to search the house as part of the game before they realised something was terribly wrong.



Police have confirmed they have launched an investigation into the tragic deaths.

In an agonising tribute, the youngsters’ mum Karen said: “Thank you my babies for having given me the greatest joy in these eight years of life.

“Thank you for having chosen me as your mother. It was the most beautiful experience I could ever have, thank you for everything we shared.

“Soon we will be together; how short time is and how long the memory lasts.

“Words fail me. I loved you as much as I could, and only God will know why He took you.



“Thank you for everything we lived and shared; you will always be in my heart for as long as it endures.”

Local mayor Juan Andres Gomez expressed his deep regrets at the tragedy and hoped nothing similar would ever happen to another family.

“This tragic event compels us to reflect as a society and to remember that protecting children is not optional; it is a duty. Children do not understand risks and rely on adult care,” he said.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“A moment of negligence can turn into an irreversible tragedy within minutes, which is why we make a firm call to parents and caregivers to maximize supervision and protection measures.

“Today, it is not enough to lament; today, we must act to ensure this does not happen again.”

News.title: Retired matador, 51, gored to death by bull while preparing for sold-out annual fight in Spain as tributes paid
News.content:
A RETIRED matador has been gored to death by a bull as he prepared for a sold-out show.

Ricardo Ortiz, 51, was severely attacked as he helped handle several raging beasts inside their enclosures ahead of an annual bullfighting event in Spain.





Ricardo was working alongside other matadors ahead of the Corrida Picassiana event held at La Malagueta in Málaga.

Lances de Futuro, the company organising the bullfight, said: “One of the bulls gave [Ortiz] a severe goring that caused his death.

“We want to convey our deepest condolences to the family, friends and colleagues of the deceased, a much-loved and respected person in the bullfighting world.”

His death reportedly came on April 3 – a day before the bullfighting event was scheduled to take place.



Lances de Futuro went ahead with the event and paid tribute to Ricardo.

A moment of silence was held at the beginning of the bullfight before three matadors took on six bulls.

Ricardo was born in Malaga in 1974 and came from a family of successful bullfighters in Spain, reports El País.

He had retired from bullfighting over two decades but had been working with Lances de Futuro helping out with various bullfighting events.



Spain is infamous for its bullfights with the country putting on 1,500 events each year.

Animal rights experts have spent decades campaigning against bullfighting due to the dangers surrounding the sport.

A month ago, a man was gored to death after being lifted up in the air on the horns of a bull at a separate event in Spain.

Shocking footage shows the worker sprinting towards metal barriers in a packed arena, glancing over his shoulder as the bull barrels towards him.

It comes just months after another fatal goring at a Spanish festival.



In September, a 57-year-old reveller was killed at the annual Toro del Gayumbo in the picturesque town of Ubrique in Cadiz province.

Video showed the man trying to scramble up metal railings as a bull named Mosquetero charged at him.

The last professional matador to die during a fight in Spain was Victor Barrio in 2016.

News.title: Gangster maniacs, $300,000 deals & chilling weapons stash – Gun dealer reveals double life before mistake exposed secret
News.content:
STORENZO Dominic was the dancer everyone noticed in New York clubs – he was the good-looking B-boy with the long hair, the local fame and the moves.

He toured, mixed with big names in the hip-hop scene and built a reputation as “that famous guy from the hood that people looked up to”.





What almost nobody knew was that he was also making quick money as a gun trafficker – moving weapons to street gangs and drug dealers and pocketing “a few $100,000” in a single transaction.

For years, he said, he hid the two lives in plain sight.

He told The Sun: “I hid it well. I never s*** where I ate.”



Dominic, who grew up in Williamsburg, Brooklyn, said his story started in a neighbourhood that looked nothing like the fashionable area it is today.

He was raised in a low-income but tight-knit Puerto Rican family, with food on the table, clothes on his back and parents who kept a close eye on him. But outside the home was a different world.

Back then, gangs were not some distant threat whispered about by adults. They were there on the block, visible every day, staking out small patches of territory and defending them with brute force.

Dominic explained: “These street gangs occupied such small pockets of the city. A quarter-mile radius – sometimes just a block or two – was their entire world, and they protected it with everything they had.”



He remembers being a boy at the window, watching gang fights unfold below.

“I would hang out my window and I would see these two gangs go into literal rumbles, you know, with zip guns and chains, bricks and knives,” he said.

“When I was there, it was strictly projects, ghettos, and gangs.

“The violence and the gang presence were constant. It was an atmosphere that was always visible to us.”

He admitted he was fascinated by it.



“Even as a kid, I was drawn to the gangs,” he said. “I was always intrigued. I wanted to be a gangster.”

But strict parents and a strong family structure stopped him going down that road as a child. He could play gangster outside, then be back upstairs for dinner at 5pm.

He thanked the rise of hip-hop and dance culture with keeping him away from the Nuyorican – the Puerto Ricans in New York.

“When dance entered the picture, it became a lifeline for us, a way to escape the influence of the gangs,” he said.

By then, in his 20s, Dominic said he had become well known in New York’s club scene.



“I became an amazing dancer. I was touring, I was popular in every club in New York City,” he recalled.

“When you hear about groups like Rock Steady, those are all my friends. We were all in it together. And I had fame. I really had fame.”

It was that fame, he said, that helped pull him back towards the street economy he had tried to leave behind.

He revealed the turning point came when he met a woman running a store near where he grew up.



“This lady was a drug dealer with her husband,” he said. “I met this one lady, and she turned me on to cocaine. So, I started doing cocaine.”

Soon he was back in the orbit of old street contacts and newer dealers too.



“They used me to get into the clubs and meet all the chicks and, you know, and because I was that popular kid,” he said.

“I never dealt drugs, it wasn’t my thing. But I was doing drugs and I was hanging out with all the dealers.”

From there, the trade crept in as a side hustle before it tightened its grip and began to define everything around him.

“I started hanging out with the wrong people, picking up guns here and there,” he said.

“It was small-time back then, just filling a need when somebody asked. I knew where to get them.”



But that “small-time” hustle didn’t stay small for long as it soon evolved into a massive interstate pipeline that moved far beyond New York City.

“By 1999, I was moving an abundance of firearms from here to Florida and Puerto Rico,” he recalled.

The scale shifted and his role was no longer peripheral, but embedded deep within the machinery.

“I was supplying the drug dealers,” he said.

“I wasn’t the ‘main guy’ at the very top, but you rule where you are. You rule your own territory.



“I had a personal arsenal that was second to none. Back then, you could pretty much get anything you wanted from me.”

He insisted he kept it all hidden from the people closest to him, adding he very rarely sold anything to anyone in his neighbourhood.

“They never really knew just how much control I had over selling. Not even my cousin.

“He was always with me, he was my best friend, and even he didn’t know. I never told them.”

At the same time, he was still dancing, bouncing at clubs and building up a public name that had nothing to do with guns.



But the gun trade was doing really well and bringing him quick money.

He said his buyers were street gangs and drug dealers – and although demand stretched as far as Puerto Rico, his core operation was closer to home in New York and New Jersey.

The supply chain behind it all, he explained, was anything but simple.

It was an irregular network pulling from multiple directions, some of it reaching beyond US borders.

“The guns were coming from overseas,” he said.



“Some of them came in from Canada. And others were from the Midwest because they were easier to get. Philadelphia, sometimes, even easier as it was so close.”

It was a system built on access and opportunity, shifting depending on what was available and where it could move most easily.

And alongside that, he maintained key relationships that kept the operation moving.

“I had that Florida connection at one point, and then I did really well shipping stuff to Puerto Rico.”

Asked how much money could be involved in one transaction, he answered: “A few $100,000.”



That secret life was running alongside another ambition: music.

After his dancing career, Dominic said he had a rap career going, with shows at the Apollo Theatre and a manager who was deeply involved in the drug trade.



Dominic would also travel with huge sums of cash.

“I would go there with $300,000 strapped on me,” he said.

“We were buying the drugs in Puerto Rico, and we would supply some of the guns.”

By March 1993, he wanted out as he had a business, a home, and enough money to leave that life behind.

But his manager persuaded him to go once more, saying he was the only one to be trusted with the job as he was no longer doing drugs.



And it did end up being his final trip, but not for a good reason.

“That’s the trip where I got bagged,” he said.

He was arrested in Puerto Rico – and had the double life he so fought to keep hidden was brutally unravelled.

“That exposed me to everyone that didn’t know that part of me… it opened up Pandora’s box,” he said.

For him, the hardest part was not the arrest itself. It was his mum finding out.



She learned of his arrest through a newspaper report.

“Not many people are called Storenzo and are from New York”, Dominic said.

“I’m a mama’s boy, I speak to my mother twice a day no matter where I go in the world.

“So she noticed right away that something was wrong, because I hadn’t called her in days.

“She was crying and couldn’t believe that her dancer son was caught up in all of this.”



Dominic said he spent about a year in Puerto Rico fighting the case – and challenging the way evidence had been gathered.

“Everyone says I was an idiot, but I decided to fight my case,” he said.

He claimed the case eventually went all the way to Puerto Rico’s Supreme Court.

He said he won, but returned home with nothing.

“When I came home, I literally had $50 in my pocket. Here I am starting all over,” he said.



It was one of the dealers who still owed him money, he said, who gave him the $5,000 foothold he needed to rebuild.

From there, he said, he built tattoo businesses and hair salons, did several acting gigs and stayed away from crime for good.

Now retired, Dominic still works two days a week in New York training new security guards and wants nothing to do with his past life.

He said: “I train up and coming security guards cause I was a bouncer for 14 years, then I did security work for years after that. So I’m still teaching the new generation how to do security.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Still true to his roots, he also runs a dance studio in New York City.



He teaches the history of specific underground dance subcultures from New York City’s 1970s and 80s, like Lofting and Electric Boogie.

News.title: Brit tourist, 42, mysteriously found dead in stairwell by girlfriend in Thailand with wound on the back of his head
News.content:
DEATH RIDDLE Brit tourist, 42, mysteriously found dead in stairwell by girlfriend in Thailand with wound on the back of his head

A BRITISH tourist has mysteriously been found dead in a stairwell in Thailand.

The Portsmouth man, 42, was discovered by his girlfriend with a wound on the back of his head, cops said.





He was allegedly drinking heavily the night before he was found and was last seen stumbling out of his rented accommodation in the notorious neighbourhood of Pattaya – aka “Sin City”.

The man’s body was found slumped and lifeless in the early hours of April 4.

Officers were called to the four-storey building around 8.30am to find the former life insurance salesman sitting motionless between the second and third floors, leaning against a railing.

He was wearing a white collared shirt and black shorts, with only one shoe on his foot.

A small wound was reportedly found on the back of his head.

Police said no signs of a struggle or forced entry were found in his room.

Police Lieutenant Akkarapong Saenputawong said: “We were initially unable to determine the cause of death.

“The body will be sent to the Institute of Forensic Medicine at the Police Hospital for a post-mortem examination.



“We are reviewing CCTV footage inside the room, and so far, we have found no abnormalities or any outsiders entering or leaving.”

He said the footage showed the man emerging shirtless from his room while intoxicated around 2am and heading down the stairwell.

The Brit was later seen returning alone before he was found dead.

His distraught girlfriend said she had returned from work when she made the grim discovery.

She told cops her boyfriend had been vomiting blood and showing signs of memory loss before his death.

News.title: Shocking moment thug threatens staff with needles and bottle of wine in Asda as thousands of shoplifters to avoid jail
News.content:
THIS is the moment a supermarket thief leaves staff terrified after threatening them with needles and a bottle of wine.

The shocking video shows Stuart Andrew Westwood, 38, entering the Asda and beginning to fill a carrier bag with various items.





When members of staff challenged him, the attacker became aggressive and pulled several needles from his pocket, threatening workers and shouting, “Don’t touch me, I’ll stab you”.

He then ran into another aisle and grabbed a bottle of wine, which he raised above his head as he moved towards the employees, threatening to use it as a weapon.

Fearing further violence, staff moved out of the way, allowing Westwood to flee with the stolen goods.

It happened at the store on Millbrook Road West, Southampton, Hants, as reported by NeedToKnow.

Following enquiries, Westwood, of no fixed abode, was later identified, arrested and charged.

He admitted robbery at a Southampton Crown Court hearing and was sentenced to 22 months in prison last week.

After sentencing, Hants Police PC Sophie Wellstead, who led the investigation, described the incident as frightening for the staff involved.



She said: “Westwood’s behaviour was volatile, intimidating and created a genuine risk of serious harm.

“I want to commend those working in the store for the calm and measured way they responded.”

She added that the sentence should reassure the public that violence and threats against retail workers will not be tolerated.

The robbery took place on January 21.

This follows recent controversy over Labour’s plans to eliminate most shoplifting prison sentences of less than a year.



This means up to 12,000 repeat offenders could soon avoid jail.

After a number of mass robbery attacks in South West London over the weekend, supermarkets have called for further powers for security guards.

Iceland boss Lord Richard Walker has spoken out about the “violent nature” of such crimes.

Walker said: “I’ve always argued for more powers for security guards. You go to Spain and all the security guards have pepper spray and a truncheon, they don’t mess about.”

The chaos in Clapham this weekend broke out after teens were rallied together on social media.

The mobs then stormed Clapham High Street twice, forcing shops to close to protect their staff and stock.

One woman told The Sun how she was locked in M&S as hundreds of youths swarmed outside the shop and had to be escorted outside by cops.

News.title: Dorset rave chaos as riot police attacked with missiles in horror violence
News.content:
Dorset rave chaos as riot police attacked with missiles in horror violence

Dorset Police said there was violence against officers at an illegal rave near East Lulworth, which attracted around 2,000 people and more than 100 vehicles on Saturday - this is a breaking story

View Image (Image: Dorset Police)

Officers in riot gear came under fire from "missiles" and faced a "violent and hostile reception" at an illegal rave in Dorset.

‌



The event near East Lulworth attracted around 2,000 people and more than 100 vehicles on Saturday. Dorset Police were called at around 11.45pm and remained on site over the weekend to ensure the event came to a "safe conclusion". Ten people were arrested for offences including driving while under the influence and assaulting an emergency worker. Police also seized equipment under Section 64 of the Criminal Justice and Public Order Act 1994.

‌



Assistant Chief Constable Steve Lyne said: "While responding to the incident, our officers came under attack from missiles and faced a violent and hostile reception.

‌



"Violence in our communities and against our officers will not be tolerated. These types of events are illegal and cause a significant disruption to communities – we must respond to ensure the safety of everyone and it is unacceptable that we are faced with violence while doing so.

"We will continue now to review evidence from the scene to identify any further offences committed and detailed enquiries will be carried out."

News.title: Killer who stabbed ex to death in frenzied attack will walk free despite appeal
News.content:
EXCLUSIVE: Killer who stabbed ex to death in frenzied attack will walk free despite appeal

Karl Oakley was given life and a minimum tariff of 15 years in 2009 after pleading guilty to the manslaughter of 18-year-old student Taylor Burrows, on the grounds of diminished responsibility

View 2 Images Karl Oakley has spent more than 17 years in prison but is now set to taste freedom after the Parole Board cleared him for release

A killer stabbed his ex-girlfriend to death in a "frenzied" knife attack - but her family's heartache has been compounded by a decision on his case.

‌



Karl Oakley, of Luton, was given life and a minimum tariff of 15 years in 2009 after pleading guilty to the manslaughter of 18-year-old student Taylor Burrows, on the grounds of diminished responsibility. Documents reveal the Parole Board directed Oakley's release last year - but the Justice Minister launched a legal challenge to block his freedom.

‌



However an panel has now upheld the decision, saying he should be granted his freedom. The Justice Secretary claiming Oakley had shown "a more entrenched pattern of verbal aggression" and had shown "abusive and aggressive behaviours towards members of staff". It was also argued the decision to release Oakley was "irrational" because the Parole Board "failed to place sufficient weight on the Respondent's continued use of verbal aggression throughout his custodial sentence when directing release".

‌



View 2 Images Taylor Burrows was staying with a friend when Oakley attacked her, stabbing her in the head, arms and body

Kim Jong-un successor named as next North Korean dictator by spy agency READ MORE :

However judicial panel member Peter Jones dismissed the appeal. He wrote: "I find that the Panel clearly set out its findings following an exercise of its judgement and properly explained its reasons for concluding that, applying the appropriate test, it was satisfied that it was no longer necessary for the protection of the public that the Respondent should be confined."

Oakley and Ms Burrows began a relationship in the spring of 2008 and he was banned from the family home when Ms Burrows started missing classes at Luton Sixth Form College. He became increasingly aggressive and, less than a week before her death, he held a knife to her throat and threatened to kill her.

‌



On February 21 2009, Oakley came to the Sainsbury's store where Miss Burrows worked, threatened her and was told to leave by security guards. She went to the house of her friend and neighbour to stay the night but Oakley forced his way into the house. Once inside he went into the kitchen and grabbed a knife.

When Miss Burrows came downstairs he jumped on her, stabbing her in the head, arms and body. She died shortly after she was rushed to hospital. Oakley fled the scene, but was later arrested.

In 2024 Oakley challenged the Ministry of Justice (MoJ) over its decision to refuse him a move to open conditions in the Court of Appeal. Lawyers argued the Parole Board had recommended he be transferred to an open prison because there was "no further work" for him to carry out inside a closed jail.

‌



But in a ruling, Lady Chief Justice Baroness Carr, sitting alongside Dame Victoria Sharp and Lord Justice William Davis, dismissed Oakley's appeal and said the MoJ's decision to reject the Parole Board's recommendation "was entirely rational". Baroness Carr said the MoJ had "considered the board's advice in detail and with care" and that the department said he must undertake further courses in prison before he could be transferred.

The court heard a panel found Oakley was "suitable for open conditions" in 2021 but this was rejected by the MoJ. A further bid was made in 2023, which was again refused in a further judgment in February 2024.

Baroness Carr said: "The Secretary of State must consider the advice of the board with care and accord it such weight as is appropriate, given the nature, extent and context of the board's findings and recommendations.

Article continues below

"But the statutory scheme is clear: the Secretary of State is the sole decision maker, and the board acts as adviser."

News.title: Teen vaped ‘every waking minute to be cool’ - then lung collapsed
News.content:
EXCLUSIVE: Teen vaped ‘every waking minute to be cool’ - then lung collapsed

Nathan Edmunds never expected to end up in hospital when he took up vaping aged just 13. But he blames the habit for a terrifying medical emergency - and is now warning against it

View 7 Images Nathan was rarely seen without puffing on a vape - but he was storing up trouble (Image: Kennedy News & Media)

A teen who started vaping to be 'cool' like his friends soon found himself doing it 'every waking moment' - until his lung collapsed.

‌



Nathan Edmunds says he started vaping when he was just 13 years old because some of his friends were at the time and he 'thought it was cool'. The 19-year-old says he started using disposable vapes, before switching to refillable pens as he got older.

‌



Nathan says his vape was constantly in his hand or his pocket - and the only time he would stop vaping was when he was asleep. The teen says vaping was the first thing he did in the morning and the last thing he did at night - and he would even go to sleep with his vape on the windowsill next to his bed.

‌



View 7 Images Nathan collapsed after vaping (Image: Kennedy News & Media)

Artemis II crew lose contact with Earth - what is happening with Moon mission READ MORE :

Bee attack leaves hiker fighting for life after being stung more than 100 times READ MORE :

Nathan, who's favourite vape flavour was strawberry kiwi, says he was woken-up by severe chest pain on December 19th 2025. He was rushed to hospital by ambulance where he was diagnosed with a collapsed right lung, which he claims doctors told him was caused by vaping.

Nathan, who would 'vape every five minutes', was kept in hospital for four days and had a chest drain fitted into his right lung. A horrifying picture shows the lad looking at the camera while exposing his side - where a draining tube can be seen going into his chest.

‌



After doctors reportedly told him his habit was the reason for his hospital admission, Nathan says he threw away his vape 'immediately'. He is now urging other teenagers to throw away their vapes 'before it's too late'.

View 7 Images He'd been vaping since he was 13 (Image: Kennedy News & Media)

Nathan, from Wolverhampton, West Midlands, said: "I was vaping from the age of 13. I thought it was cool and some of my friends were doing it so I picked one up, tried it and it just stuck about. I got addicted to it very quickly."

‌



Nathan says he switched from disposable to refillable vapes as he got older, and would refill his vape up to three times per day.

Nathan said: "I would refill my vape two or three times a day easily. I was constantly picking it up, every five minutes, having a few drags. It [my vape] was always in my hand or in my pocket, it was never left by itself really. The only time I really stopped using it was sleeping.

View 7 Images Nathan's lung was horrendously damaged (Image: Kennedy News & Media)

‌



"Just before I'd go to sleep I'd have my last drag, put it on my windowsill. When I'd wake up, I'd pick it back up and then I'd just carry on using it. My favourite flavours were strawberry kiwi and lemon and lime."

Nathan was rushed to hospital by ambulance on December 19th 2025 after he was woken-up by severe chest pain.

Nathan said: "My lung collapsed while I was sleeping - that's the scariest part about it. There were no pain symptoms and no warning. It was just the pain from my lung collapsing woke me up at about 6am in the morning."

‌



Nathan claims doctors told him that the lung collapse had been caused by vaping. Nathan said: "The doctors said it was due to the vaping. The vape coats your lungs in oils.

View 7 Images He spent four days in hospital (Image: Kennedy News & Media)

"It was a bit of a relief because the first thing that was going through my head was lung cancer, but I always like to prepare for the worst. So when they said it was a lung collapse it was a shock.

‌



"I didn't think it would happen [to me] - I saw it obviously happening to other people but I used to say it wouldn't happen to me. Everyone says that until it happens to you."

Nathan stayed in hospital for four days and was treated with a chest drain to help his lung to reinflate. He said: "I had a chest drain put into my right lung to get rid of anything from my chest cavity.

View 7 Images Fluid was drained from his lung (Image: Kennedy News & Media)

‌



"Luckily I didn't need to have surgery because it healed very quickly. The time when it was happening it was near enough Christmas and they wanted to get me out as quick as possible.

"If the chest drain wasn't working fast enough then they would have done a surgery but l got lucky and the hole healed itself very quickly."

After finding out that vaping was responsible for his hospital admission, Nathan 'immediately' threw away his vape. Nathan said: "I stopped vaping completely after this happened. I packed it all in straight away.

‌



"Obviously when it all happened, because we didn't know what it was at first, I was still vaping at the hospital. When I got told, I chucked it in the bin there and then."

View 7 Images Nathan is warning people against vaping (Image: Kennedy News & Media)

After quitting vaping himself almost two months ago, Nathan is now warning other teenagers to throw away their vapes 'before it's too late'.

Article continues below

Nathan said: "Pack it in before it's too late. I said the same that it wouldn't happen to me, but it will.

"Replace it with something - for me if I ever do get a craving, I'll have a sweet. Chuck it [your vape] in the bin while you can. It's not worth it, just to have a bit of a fruity flavour in your mouth or have a nicotine rush."

News.title: Dad 'left to rot' in Co-Op funeral home as horrified family 'robbed of goodbye'
News.content:
Dad 'left to rot' in Co-Op funeral home as horrified family 'robbed of goodbye'

Kevin Fairfield's family claim the Co-Op 'robbed' them of their 'chance to say goodbye' by failing to embalm him or even find a coffin after he died at home unexpectedly aged 65

View 5 Images Kevin Fairfield died at home aged 65 - but his family say they 'robbed' of the chance to say goodbye (Image: Supplied)

A devastated family have told the Mirror how their their beloved dad was ‘left to rot’ in a Co-Op funeral home.

‌



Kevin Fairfield died suddenly at his home in Rosyth, near Dunfermline aged 65 after suffering a heart attack - leaving his family stricken with grief and desperate to give him a proper send-off. But their pain turned to “trauma” over what they say happened next - a “horrific failure of care” by staff at a Co-Operative funeral home, who they claim failed to do even basic preparation of his body after nearly two weeks, and did not even find him a coffin.

‌



Their dad's body was not embalmed despite their requests, and was allowed to decompose to a state where they were advised not see him, leaving the close-knit family feeling “robbed of their goodbyes”.

‌



View 5 Images Kali Hope, Keiron Fairfield, Kev Fairfield (son), Kevin Fairfield (father) (Image: Supplied)

Families conned by funeral director Robert Bush heckle and chase him from court READ MORE :

Bodycam footage shows Robert Bush arrested on American Airlines plane at Heathrow READ MORE :

Kevin's children eventually made alternative plans with a local, family-run funeral home, whose staff were the first outside of the Co-Op to see the “absolutely brutal” state he had been left in.

On July 21, 2024, when the retired HGV driver was found dead at home by his eldest child Keiron, the rest of the family, including 38-year-old son Kev and youngest daughter Kali Hope, 34, rushed home to be with him.

‌



By the time Kali arrived, paramedics and police were already outside the house, and it had been agreed that her dad would be taken directly to the mortuary due to the nature of his death, which was deemed “not police reportable”. She said the Co-Operative Funeralcare in Rosyth, Fife, was mentioned by an officer at the scene, as the force has an existing contract with the funeral home for police reportable deaths.

But their suspicions about the Co Op’s service began early on, when Kev said a funeral employee told him over the phone that they “would not be collecting the body” because it was a Sunday afternoon - a situation he claims only changed when he handed the phone to a policeman. The Co-Op deny this version of events, and told the Mirror that they would “never” refuse to collect a deceased person.

In the days that followed, Kali, Kev other members of the family called multiple times to ask when they would be able to see their dad in a chapel of rest - and grew increasingly worried about the lack of information given in return. “It felt like a transaction, rather than the personal touch that they promise you - they’d done absolutely nothing“, Kali said.

‌



View 5 Images Kevin's family said Co-Op Funeralcare branch in Rosyth left his body in an 'absolutely brutal' state (Image: Google)

By August 2, the family had become so frustrated that they made arrangements for Kevin to be transferred to the independent firm Callum Robertson Funeral Directors, who would go on to organise the memorial service. When two workers from the firm arrived as arranged on Friday 2 August to collect him - thirteen days after Kevin had died - they were told they would need to wait at reception, a situation that continued for “two hours“ with little explanation.

Kali explained that the funeral workers eventually went inside to find a Co-Op employee hurriedly cleaning Kevin’s body, and immediately noticed he was “severely decomposed”. He did not have a coffin, wasn't embalmed as the family had requested, and had only just been changed out of the clothes he died in - despite his children having provided a suit for him several days earlier.

‌



Kev said: “They witnessed them [Co-Op staff] cleaning dad's body, so essentially doing the first clean 13 days after, or 12 days after he'd been gone into their care, and he hadn't been embalmed.”

Kali added: “His clothes were actually in a biohazard bag right next to him that he'd passed away in, they had just taken the clothes off him. So he'd lain in those clothes from the Sunday until the Friday after, in the clothes he passed away in.“

View 5 Images His daughter Kali said 'nobody deserves to be treated the way that he was' (Image: Supplied)

‌



The new funeral directors were able to take hair cuttings and fingerprints, but due to the decomposed state of Kevin’s body - details of which the family still find too upsetting for us to publish - they were told it would be too distressing for them to see him before he was cremated. Legal letters were exchanged in the months after the funeral service, and eventually the Co-op agreed to an out-of-court financial settlement with the family, which Kali confirmed was a ”five-figure sum”.

During the dispute, the family discovered that the Co-Op had listed the wrong height for their dad in their records. Without any explanation other than a “procedural error”, it left them tortured by their own imaginations as to what had gone wrong. Kev explained: “Basically nothing was done right.

“We received two separate timelines from them, both with very differing accounts. In one of the timelines they've got dad listed as being 6’2. Dad was about 5’8. One of the timelines states that his coffin was closed, but we never had a coffin. They told us they couldn't get a coffin for him."

‌



“They put on the report that they ‘lost to a competitor’ - no reasoning or anything - and then about six months down the line they sent us a satisfaction survey by email,“ he added. But they're now determined to share how their dad was failed after he died - not just because of the emotional impact on themselves, which has led several members of the family to undergo NHS counselling, but to ensure that no other families have to deal with what they did.

Kev said: “There's a lot of mental health issues that have been exacerbated because of this. A lot of that stemmed from not knowing, but also from creating scenarios in our head.”

View 5 Images Kevin had coached local youth football teams and was an HGV driver before his health suffered in his 60s (Image: Supplied)

‌



Kali added: “Nobody deserves to be treated the way that he was. If something can come of it, and that's all we want, we'd take that as a kind of victory for us after being through all this - that nobody else has to go through it. It's hard enough losing a parent, but having to sit and plan the funeral twice, is just something nobody should go through.

"We've never had that time with dad after he passed, in a nice environment like what you're supposed to do, we've had that taken away and nobody can ever give us that back."

Kali described her late father as the “biggest joker”, recalling how he “travelled the world ” and “always had a story to tell”. Kev said his dad “genuinely did care about everybody”, and had helped coach youth football teams before his health struggles began towards his 60s. As they carry on their lives with the pain of being “denied” the goodbye their father deserved, the family are calling for change in the way the funeral sector is regulated - a system which they claim allows directors to effectively “mark their own homework”.

‌



In Scotland, a law brought in since Mr Fairfield’s death means funeral homes are now required to be a member of one of several different trade associations, rather than a government or independent regulator. The UK government is currently reviewing regulation of the sector in England after a string of scandals, including the conviction this week of funeral director Robert Bush, 48, who admitted to preventing the burial of 30 bodies at his parlour in Hull.

The NAFD, one of Britain’s largest industry associations, refused to handle the complaint from Kevin’s family because they hadn't paid the final bill to the Co-op but to the second, non-member firm - a state of affairs his son Kev describes as “not good enough”. He said: “There has to be an independent body. There has to be an independent organisation that funeral homes have to answer to. One that they have no influence over, that they're not a part of it, where they're not funding it."

An NAFD spokesperson told the Mirror: “In line with our practices, we offer a route for any complaint through NAFD Resolve, our comprehensive and independent dispute resolution service. However, because the family quickly moved the funeral to a non-member firm and the funeral did not proceed with the NAFD member firm, a route through NAFD Resolve was not applicable. The family then settled directly with the member firm. At no point did we refuse to investigate a complaint against a member firm.”

Article continues below

A spokesperson for the Co-Op Funeralcare told the Mirror that they had apologised to the family for the “procedural error“. The spokesperson added: “We are committed to delivering the highest standards of professionalism, service and care for the thousands of bereaved families and their loved ones that we serve across the nation.

“On this occasion, we recognise that we did not meet these high standards due to a procedural error and for this we sincerely apologise. However, we are confident that Mr Fairfield was treated with the utmost dignity and respect during his time in our care. Following an investigation, actions were taken internally to prevent this from happening again and we also provided Mr Fairfield’s family with a full detailed timeline and summary of our findings.”

News.title: Woman spends £600 taking limping cat to the vet and then makes realisation
News.content:
Woman spends £600 taking limping cat to the vet and then makes realisation

A cat owner who spent £600 on vet fees after noticing her pet was limping has made a shocking discovery about her cat's health - but it's not what she expected

View Image The woman took her cat to the vet before her realisation (stock photo) (Image: jamesjoong/ iStock via Getty Images)

Noticing something different about your cat's behaviour can easily make you panic.

‌



As much as we wish our pets could talk to us, they cannot tell us how they're feeling or why they might be acting a little bit strange one day. So, we have to use our best judgment and take them to the vet if we believe they need treatment, even if it turns out that their behaviour was caused by something completely benign.

‌



This is the situation one cat owner found herself in recently when she rushed her ginger cat to the vet after she noticed he was limping. The woman paid £600 in vet fees to get him looked at, but it wasn't until she got the cat home that she made a shocking discovery about his health.

‌



In a video shared on TikTok, the woman said that just 24 hours after their vet visit, her cat was acting like a completely different animal - and there seemed to be nothing wrong with him at all.

The cat, which is one of three that the woman owns, was filmed racing around her home, jumping off the walls, standing on the top of her doors, and rolling around on the floor, all within hours of limping around so much that the woman had to take him to the vet to be checked over.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



She wrote on her video: "My cat the day after I spent £600 at the vet because he was limping."

The woman didn't explain what the outcome of her vet visit was, so it's unknown whether her cat was given any treatment for his limp or if the vet was able to explain why her pet was limping.

Commenters on the post could sympathise with the woman's plight, however, as many of them said they had also spent hundreds of pounds in vet fees just to have the vet tell them that their cat is perfectly healthy.

‌



One person said: "Mine kept holding his paw up, I took him to the vet's thinking it was a sprain, then realised he holds his paw up every time he's hungry."

Another added: "My cat eating a full serving of food the first time in a month after spending $400 (£300) at the vet. I think she heals every time I spend money on her."

Why is my cat limping?

According to Pet MD, you should never ignore your cat if it's limping. It can be a sign of pain, so taking your animal to the vet is always advised to ensure there's nothing serious going on.

‌



Some potential causes of limping can include:

A broken bone

A dislocated joint

A torn toenail

An insect sting or bite

Bruising

Infections affecting soft tissue, bones, or joints

Osteoarthritis

Autoimmune or inflammatory disease

Cancer affecting bones, soft tissue, or joints

If you notice your cat is limping, Pet MD suggests gently examining the problem area to see if you can spot any issues with their toenails, paw pads, feet, and legs. However, if your cat resists this, don't push it.

Article continues below

You should also keep your cat indoors so you can monitor them more closely and encourage them to rest. If your cat's symptoms don't improve after a couple of days, or they get worse, make an appointment with your vet.

For more information, visit the Pet MD website.

News.title: 'I was so hooked on drugs I was going to die - then a coma changed everything'
News.content:
EXCLUSIVE: 'I was so hooked on drugs I was going to die - then a coma changed everything'

Gram Seed, now 61, became addicted to drugs when he was a teenager, which spurred him on to a life of crime, but visions during a six-day coma left him ready to turn his life around for good

Former football hooligan Gram Seed discusses how he turned his life around after a six-day coma'

Gram Seed carries his history on his skin - knife scars across his chest, a dismembered chin, and missing fingers.

‌



But at 61, the former football hooligan is a world away from his former self, who was addicted to crack cocaine and heroin, and nearly had his life support switched off. After a miraculous recovery from a six-day coma that followed a total organ collapse, the dad-of-two has transformed from a violent criminal into a relentlessly hopeful figure, who has dedicated his life to rescuing others from the same darkness that once consumed him.

‌



Speaking to the Mirror, Gram says he endured visions during that coma that inspired him to turn his life around. Today, he describes himself simply as "a messenger" after transforming his life by helping others escape the same darkness that once consumed him.

‌



Easter bank holiday 2026 opening times for Sainsbury's as hours set to change READ MORE :

American tries a custard cream for the first time but is confused by 1 thing READ MORE :

View 7 Images Gram began getting himself in trouble as a youngster (Image: Supplied)

Gram's descent into crime began as a "mischevious" child" on a council estate in Middlesbrough, but it quickly escalated into a cycle of robbery, prison and brutal violence.

"I was just a mischievous child," he recalls. "Nickin' things off washing lines, stealing from corner shops, petty crimes."

‌



By the age of 13, he had fallen in with a gang, boxing and playing rugby by day but committing robberies and assaults by night. A turning point came after visiting his grandmother, one of the most important parental figures in his life, in a hospital.

"I remember thinking I was sick of crying," he says. "I just went cold. I didn't care about people anymore."

View 7 Images He now hopes to help others escape addiction and violence (Image: Andy Commins)

‌



By 16, Gram was in a detention centre after breaking into schools and youth clubs. But instead of rehabilitation, he found a system built on discipline and punishment.

"There was no help," he says. "It was all about running fences and wearing uniforms." Within months of release, he was back behind bars - this time linked to football violence.

His life became a cycle of crime, prison and instability. He was stabbed multiple times, attacked at matches and left with permanent injuries - including losing part of his finger and chin.

‌



View 7 Images The teen was brought up on a council estate (Image: Supplied)

At one point, he was even questioned in connection with a death during a nightclub riot. "I was right at the front," he says. "People blamed me because they saw me."

He was later cleared, but by then, his life was already entrenched in chaos. By the early 1990s, everything had fallen apart. His family had distanced themselves, his grandmother had died, and the home he once owned was gone.

‌



He drifted between houses before ending up on the streets where addiction took hold. "I was taking heroin and crack cocaine. I was robbing for it all," he says.

In February 1993, sitting on a bench in Middlesbrough, he made a decision. "I decided I was going to die there," he says. "Live there, die there."

For years, he barely ate, his body slowly shutting down under the weight of drugs, alcohol and neglect. On 9 August 1996, Gram collapsed on the bench.

‌



View 7 Images He completely turned his life around after coming out of a coma (Image: Andy Commins)

Rushed to hospital with organ failure, pneumonia, hypothermia and severe malnutrition, d octors gave him little chance of survival as he slipped into a six day coma.

After doctors asked his mother to sign the papers to switch off his life support, she spent a few hours deliberating - during which time, members of a Christian group that knew Gram from the streets prayed by his bedside.

‌



While unconscious, he experienced vivid, almost surreal experiences that he believes fundamentally rewired his brain.

He said: " At first, I was in a room and everything was brilliant white and there was two people cleaning up and a fan blowing air on me.

View 7 Images Gram with wife Natasha who he met through the church (Image: Supplied)

‌



"Then, I went from there to a mountain. I was dripping with wax and then a big sound came and it put me in this water, that was pure, beautiful water and then I woke up."

"I said straight away, 'I'm never going to drink or take drugs again."

‌



Gram was certain that from that moment his life had changed for good. Just weeks after leaving hospital, he found himself looking out at the same streets he once lived on - watching others trapped in addiction.

"I wanted to cry," he says. "But it was tears of 'I want to help them'." He began attending courses, eventually committing to his faith later that year.

View 7 Images The pair married a year after they first met (Image: Andy Commins)

‌



By November 1996, he was back on the same bench where he once expected to die, but this time, sharing a message of hope. "I didn’t know how to pray or read the Bible," he says. "But I knew something was real."

After taking an Alpha course, a programme that introduces people to the basics of Christianity, Gram began working across rehabilitation services in prisons and schools.

Since then, he has developed anti-bullying initiatives within schools; facilitated workshops supporting those with substance abuse; supported chaplaincy services across adult and youth custodial settings; contributed to faith-based rehabilitation programmes; and served as the official chaplain for nine years at a secure training centre for young offenders.

‌



Gram then met his now wife Natasha while attending a church in London. The pair married in 1999 and went on to have two sons, Caleb and Boaz.

View 7 Images Caleb and Boaz, Natasha and Gram's sons (Image: Supplied)

He describes their upbringing as "black and white" compared to his own - with neither having been involved in crime or drugs and going on to attend university.

‌



Natasha now runs a charity supporting vulnerable women, while Gram continues his work mentoring people from all walks of life. Today, Gram works with everyone from those sleeping rough to successful professionals.

"I’m just a big arrow pointing in a different direction," he explains. "I like to help people get found." And for those who know his story, one phrase has come to define him.

"Someone once shouted to me outside a prison - 'Gram, you're hope on legs'," he says. "That's how I’d like to be remembered."

News.title: Harry and William 'strain' over major royal event that poses difficult dilemma for Firm
News.content:
EXCLUSIVE: Harry and William 'strain' over major royal event that poses difficult dilemma for Firm

A royal wedding is on the horizon, and while the event will be a happy occasion for the Royal Family, the rift between the Prince of Wales and the Duke of Sussex could prove to be a problem

View 4 Images Prince William and Prince Harry may not get an invite to their cousin's wedding due to their rift (Image: Martin Meissner/AP/REX/Shutterstock)

A royal wedding is just around the corner, as Princess Anne’s son Peter Phillips revealed the date for his nuptials with NHS nurse Harriet Sperling. Earlier this week, Peter announced that their summer wedding will take place on Saturday, June 6 in a private ceremony at All Saints Church, Kemble in Cirencester.

‌



The couple say that the King and Queen as well as the Prince and Princess of Wales have also been informed of the announcement and that further details will be announced in due course. And while a royal wedding is a joyous occasion, a royal expert believes Prince Harry and Prince William ’s rift could be a problem.

‌



Should Prince Harry be invited to Sandringham this summer? Take our poll and have your say READ MORE :

View 4 Images Peter Phillips with wife-to-be Harriet Sperling (Image: PA)

‌



Peter and Harriet have been together since the spring of 2024, with the NHS nurse, who is also a single mother to a teenage daughter from a previous relationship, showing up for royal events over the last year. Just yesterday, they joined the rest of the Royal Family for annual Easter Sunday celebrations, along with Harriet's teenage daughter Georgina.

According to former BBC royal correspondent Jennie Bond, the wedding of Peter and Harriet will be a welcome change from the current turmoil for the Royal Family. She told the Mirror : “A wedding is always a happy distraction, and the news of Peter and Harriet’s wedding will have been welcomed by the family.

“She has already proved quite a hit, especially with her future sister-in-law, Zara, and husband Mike Tindall. I think they’re very wise to have a private ceremony… with the way things are, it will take a huge amount of strain away from what will hopefully be the happiest day of their lives.”

‌



While the ceremony will be a small and private affair, it is unclear which members of the Royal Family will get an invitation. Many have already started to speculate whether Peter will invite his first cousins Harry and William, given their years long estrangement.

View 4 Images Harry and William have been estranged for several years (Image: POOL/AFP via Getty Images)

As Jennie explained: “There is, of course, the dilemma about whether William or Harry or both should be invited. Peter has been a great support over the years to both of them. He walked between them as a sort of buffer at the late Duke of Edinburgh’s funeral and was a shoulder for them to cry on after their mother’s death.

‌



“The rift between the brothers must be difficult for Peter to negotiate. But he now has the get-out clause of saying this is just a small private wedding and thus excusing both William and Harry from attending.”

Jennie believes Harriet, who will be Peter’s second wife, has been welcomed into the Royal Family with open arms, particularly by Princess Kate, given the two women’s shared interest in children's development.

View 4 Images Peter and Harriet will tie the knot on June 6 (Image: Victoria Jones/Shutterstock)

‌



“Harriet does seem to have slotted into her semi-royal life with Peter very easily,” Jennie said. “She has looked elegant and at ease in the company of the rest of the Royals and I’m sure she will have the respect of Catherine in particular.

“As an NHS paediatric nurse who is particularly interested in early brain development in babies and in ensuring that children thrive, she will have much in common with the Princess. I think she’ll be a welcome addition to the wider family.”

News.title: Duchess of Edinburgh's 'secret turmoil over Andrew' as she skips Easter service
News.content:
Duchess of Edinburgh's 'secret turmoil over Andrew' as she skips Easter service

Sophie, Duchess of Edinburgh, was a no-show at the royals' Easter Matins service. This weekend, her husband, Prince Edward, became the first royal to visit disgraced Andrew Mountbatten Windsor in Sandringham

View 4 Images Sophie, Duchess of Edinburgh, is a well loved member of the Firm (Image: Getty)

The royals were out in full force this Easter weekend - but one key player was notably absent.

‌



Sophie, Duchess of Edinburgh, had been expected to be among the members of the Firm joining the King, Queen and the Prince and Princess of Wales for the annual Easter Matins service at Windsor Castle on Sunday.

‌



But despite both her husband Prince Edward being there with their son James, the Earl of Wessex, Sophie did not join them. It is believed that she decided against attending the service as she is 'under the weather'.

‌



It was likely a blow for Charles, as Sophie and Edward have become ever more important in supporting the monarchy with the depletion of working royals.

The Firm are also still grappling with the Andrew Mountbatten Windsor 'problem' as he is said to be "digging his heels" over moving to his permanent Sandringham residence of Marsh Farm.

View 4 Images The royals walking to church on Easter Sunday (Image: PA)

‌



The disgraced former prince has been living at Marsh Farm, another one of Charles' private properties on the estate, since being booted out Royal Lodge - his 30-room mansion in Windsor.

His younger brother, Prince Edward, became the "first and only" Windsor to go and see Andrew in Sandringham this weekend, to have a "quiet word" about hurrying up his move.

Edward and Sophie often use Wood Farm as their Easter break property, but this year they reportedly had to fork out for a holiday let because the ex duke "refused to budge" from his temporary pad.

‌



"He is just going back and forth between Wood Farm and Marsh Farm," a source told the Sun. "It's got to be sorted as Edward and Sophie like to use Wood Farm."

View 4 Images Prince Edward went to visit his disgraced brother Andrew (Image: PA)

The couple play a vital role in representing the Firm at public events, with royal expert Jennie Bond telling the Mirror that the Duke and Duchess of Edinburgh could be the saviours of the monarchy after Andrew's fall from grace.

‌



She told us last month: "With the depletion of the working royals, Edward and Sophie have become ever more important in supporting the monarchy. And I’m sure they will continue to have key roles when William becomes King.

"Sophie, in particular, has a girl-next-door charm about her that she has never lost, even though she is now a very senior member of the royal family. She is immensely relatable, with no airs or graces, and she has a close and very relaxed relationship with her nephew, William."

"I'm sure that Edward and Sophie discuss everything and provide valuable support to one another in this crisis", Jennie explained. "As the two youngest sons of the late Queen – both of them a decade or more younger than their siblings - Edward and Andrew probably have the closest bond.

‌



View 4 Images A photo of Andrew on all fours over a female, released in the Epstein files (Image: DoJ)

"So it has no doubt been hard for Edward to witness his brother's disgrace. But his first and overriding loyalty is to his wife, who is such a tireless campaigner for women who have been sexually abused, particularly in the war zones of the world. How utterly depressing it must be for Sophie to learn about the long-standing and close friendship between her brother-in-law and a convicted paedophile."

Last month, Edward became the first senior member of the Royal Family to be challenged about his brother following the release of millions of documents in the Epstein files. During a trip to Dubai in February, he said it was "really important" to Epstein's victims.

And Jennie added: "I have no doubt that Edward was absolutely sincere when he said that it was really important always to remember the victims, especially as he has watched and admired his wife’s work campaigning for many years against sexual violence.

"And of course, he's right. At least he spoke up - and that's what we need from the family instead of the old, outdated strategy of 'never complain, never explain'."

News.title: What next for Deontay Wilder? The Anthony Joshua problem in his way
News.content:

And still those voices are calling from far away. The familiar lyrics of The Eagles’ “Hotel California” echoed around the O2 Arena during one final, stirring Derek Chisora ring walk. Wake you up in the middle of the night, just to hear them say... “BOOOOOMB SQUAAAAAAD!”

This was the familiar refrain of Deontay Wilder, screeching over Chisora’s post-fight interview after edging past the Briton in a brutal, draining duel under the iconic dome. Chisora’s fairytale farewell was not to be on Saturday, with the veteran hitting the canvas before two of the three scorecards favoured his American opponent.

And so, a 42-year-old Chisora will (reluctantly) leave boxing behind, at least the dangerous side of the ropes, while a 40-year-old Wilder battles on. Would this future have been the same if had the result been reversed?

open image in gallery Deontay Wilder celebrates a narrow win over Derek Chisora ( Getty Images )

It’s hard to say. Chisora claimed before the bout that he would retire regardless, which was and is the right call, but you never know with “Delboy”. Wilder seemed more defiant, despite his waning powers and worsening record. With that in mind, perhaps even defeat might not have marked the end for the ex-heavyweight champion.

And he certainly appears intent on channeling this victory – as slight as it was – into more success. Just ask Anthony Joshua.

“Let’s do it,” were Wilder’s words to his old rival on Saturday, as the American navigated his way out of the O2 and past his fellow former champion. Joshua, 36, was making his first public appearance in the UK since December, when he survived a fatal car crash in Nigeria, which claimed the lives of two of his close friends.

With that tragic incident still fresh in the mind, there are those who believe “AJ” should call time on his own storied career. Yet the Briton will return to the ring, his promoter has confirmed, with a summer comeback on the cards after he dismantled YouTuber Jake Paul four months ago.

So, here we are, with arguments abounding that Joshua and Wilder should each retire, yet with both linked once more.

“You ain’t ready for that,” Joshua replied after Wilder’s comment, with the American walking off and sniping: “He’s scared as f***.” It was one of Wilder’s tamer comments on a week of stupefying ones.

Joshua vs Wilder has been mooted for the best part of a decade, but it was never closer than in 2023, when they shared a ring. They did not share the ring as opponents, instead boxing one after the other; Joshua took apart Otto Wallin, but only after Wilder faltered against Joseph Parker. If both had won, they would have met in two contracted fights, per Wilder.

He could not uphold his end of the bargain and went on to lose to Zhilei Zhang, while Joshua knocked out ex-UFC champion Francis Ngannou. But Joshua and Wilder’s fortunes would reverse yet again, when AJ was brutally beaten by Daniel Dubois in 2024 and Wilder stopped Tyrrell Anthony Herndon last summer. With each man adding another win since then, it feels like a showdown could be sold once more.

Should it be, however?

open image in gallery Wilder vs Chisora brought chaos, with one of the Briton’s coaches entering the ring in round one ( Adam Davy/PA Wire )

Firstly, Joshua seems to be on a different path, with his planned summer fight likely serving as a warm-up to a clash with Tyson Fury. Yes, that fight – even more craved and elusive than Joshua vs Wilder – is on the cards again. And even if Joshua vs Wilder could be lined up, would it be the right move?

Joshua would be the favourite at this point, but it shouldn’t be forgotten that his sole win in the last two years came against an influencer-turned-boxer, and that we still don’t know where his head is at (most recently, he’s been training with former opponent Oleksandr Usyk in Ukraine). Meanwhile, there was plenty of criticism of Wilder in the wake of his win over Chisora, including those afore-mentioned calls for his retirement.

This writer saw it slightly differently. Yes, Wilder’s performance was flawed, but he looked much less gun-shy and much more resilient than in recent outings. When you weigh up every factor on his side and on Joshua’s, it feels like they might just balance out.

That said, one of Wilder’s post-fight comments contradicted the idea that he was more trigger-happy: “I held back a couple of times, because when I cut his eye open, I started thinking about him being with his children, and when I saw veins coming out of his temple...” Still, that’s not what we saw. Furthermore, Wilder and Chisora are friends, and the “Bronze Bomber” would surely show no mercy to AJ.

open image in gallery Chisora was knocked through the ropes in the eighth round ( Getty Images )

Again, though, it should be noted that Joshua appears to have other options. Does Wilder?

He has talked up a world-title fight, which will almost certainly not come. Just a few months ago, unified champ Oleksandr Usyk hinted at a voluntary defence against Wilder, but it will instead come against kickboxer Rico Verhoeven, and Usyk will then be forced into a mandatory defence. The only other heavyweight world title is held by Fabio Wardley, who will defend it against Daniel Dubois in May, and it would be a farce for Wilder to challenge the winner.

However, a fight between Wilder and the loser of Wardley vs Dubois appeals.

At this point, Wilder will not risk his boxing future against anyone who is not a champion or a top name, which leaves him with very few options. For better of worse, Joshua remains the most-interesting option of all.

The chief of intelligence of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) was killed in an airstrike on Monday, state media said.

Majid ⁠Khademi, who accused Donald Trump of fuelling anti-government protests in Iran, is the latest key figure to have been killed in strikes since the US-Israel war on the Islamic Republic began on 28 February.

The Israeli military on Monday claimed it killed Khademi, along with another top IRGC officer, in overnight strikes. “Khademi was one of the IRGC’s most senior commanders and had accumulated extensive experience over many years,” the IDF wrote on X.

Israel also claimed it killed Yazdan Mir, known by his alias Sardar Bagheri, who headed the IRGC Quds Force’s clandestine Unit 840. They were reported to be among at least 25 people killed in overnight strikes on Iran after Trump threatened to turn the country into “hell” if it refused to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

The IRGC confirmed Khademi’s death, saying that the “powerful and educated” head of its Intelligence Organisation was “martyred in the criminal terrorist attack by the American-Zionist enemy... at dawn today”.

Israel's defence minister Israel Katz said after Khademi’s death that his country would “continue to hunt them down one by one”, referring to Iran’s senior leadership.

Khademi replaced his predecessor, Mohammad Kazemi, in 2025 after he was killed during the 12-day Iran-Israel war. He spent decades ‌in intelligence and counter-espionage ‌roles while rising through Iran’s security apparatus.

Before his appointment, Khademi ⁠headed the Guards' Intelligence Protection Organisation 2022 onwards, charged with internal surveillance and counter-intelligence, and held senior roles in Iran’s defence ministry.

The IRGC intelligence arm is ‌one of Iran’s most ​powerful security bodies, with ‌a central ⁠role in domestic surveillance ⁠to counter foreign influence, and often ‌operating in ​parallel with the ‌civilian intelligence ministry.

Israel has relentlessly targeted key figures in Iran’s political and military leadership, including supreme leader Ali Khamenei, who was among the first victims of the US-Israeli strikes that started the war on 28 February.

Other senior figures killed in strikes since then include security chief Ali Larijani and the Guards' commander-in-chief Mohammad Pakpour. Basij commander Gholamreza Soleimani and IRGC spokesperson Ali Mohammad Naini have also been killed in Israeli strikes.

Trump has threatened to escalate American attacks on Tehran if a deal has not been reached to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, a vital shipping route for oil and gas, by 8pm EST on Tuesday. In an expletive-laden post on his platform Truth Social, Trump said the US would start hitting power plants and bridges to send Iran “back to the Stone Age”, adding: “Open the F***** Strait, you crazy ba*****, or you'll be living in Hell - JUST WATCH.”

Amid reports that Iranian officials are reluctant to take part in face-to-face peace talks over fears they too could be assassinated, Trump said late on Sunday that negotiators would be granted “immunity from death”.

Iran’s parliamentary speaker Mohammad Bagher Qalibaf called the threat to target Iran’s civilian infrastructure “reckless”. “You won’t gain anything through war crimes,” Qalibaf wrote on X. “The only real solution is respecting the rights of the Iranian people and ending this dangerous game.”

In an effort to stop the fighting, Egyptian, Pakistani and Turkish mediators have sent Iran and the US a joint proposal calling for a 45-day ceasefire and the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz to give time to try and find a way to end the war.

But Iran swiftly rejected the proposal, saying it will not reopen the Strait of Hormuz in exchange for a “temporary ceasefire”.
